descriptions./about/: RECR helps real-estate investors find the right capital path — transaction-first review across fix-and-flip, DSCR rental, bridge, construction, 2–4 unit, and purchase-rehab structures.
descriptions./accessibility/: Accessibility commitment and contact for Real Estate Capital Resources web properties.
descriptions./bridge/: Short-term bridge financing for property investors when speed matters and a clean exit is defined up front. See how the exit is underwritten and when it fits.
descriptions./cleveland-real-estate-investor-financin: Business-purpose financing guidance for Cleveland and Northeast Ohio real estate investors, including fix-and-flip, DSCR rental, bridge, construction, 2–4 unit and purchase-rehab transactions.
descriptions./contact/: Contact Real Estate Capital Resources — phone 954-676-4205, Cleveland and South Florida markets, deal submission.
descriptions./disclosures/: Legal and program disclosures for Real Estate Capital Resources marketing materials and website.
descriptions./experienced/: Capital-path guidance for experienced real estate investors scaling flips, rentals, rehabs, and construction — faster files when the track record is real.
descriptions./faq/: Answers about RECR capital paths, the shared-economics structure, documentation, markets, and how deal review works.
descriptions./first-time/: Capital path guidance for first-time fix-and-flip and rental investors — what files need, what experience means, and how to avoid the wrong product.
descriptions./fix-and-flip/: Fix and flip loans for purchase and renovation of investment property. How deals are evaluated, how rehab draws work, and how to submit a project for review.
descriptions./ground-up/: Ground-up construction financing built around plans, budgets, and a milestone draw schedule. See how draws release, what underwriting checks, and when it fits.
descriptions./how-it-works/: How RECR reviews investor real-estate deals — from first numbers to capital path, documentation, and clear-to-close coordination.
descriptions./: Business-purpose financing for real estate investors, including fix-and-flip, DSCR rental, purchase-and-rehab, bridge, ground-up construction, and 2–4 unit multifamily. Bring RECR the deal and we'll help identify the right capital path.
descriptions./loan-products/: Compare RECR financing programs for real estate investors: fix and flip, DSCR rental, purchase and rehab, bridge, ground-up construction, and 2-4 unit multifamily.
descriptions./multifamily/: Financing for duplex, triplex, and fourplex residential investment properties within RECR's 1-4 unit investor universe. Distinct from single-asset DSCR framing.
descriptions./partners/: Capital resource for mortgage brokers, agents, wholesalers, builders, attorneys, and professional referral partners.
descriptions./privacy/: Privacy policy for Real Estate Capital Resources — what we collect, how deal data is handled, and analytics.
descriptions./purchase-rehab/: Purchase and major renovation financing for investment property. RECR helps evaluate basis, rehab budget, ARV, and private-lender path fit without fixed marketing leverage percentages.
descriptions./rental/: DSCR rental loans for 1-4 unit investment properties, qualified on the property's cash flow not your income. See how DSCR is calculated and when it fits.
descriptions./resources/bridge-exit-risk/: A bridge loan is only as strong as its exit. How refinance and sale takeouts differ, where timeline risk hides, and how to prove your exit before you borrow.
descriptions./resources/bridge-to-dscr/: How bridge financing and DSCR rental financing work together when acquisition or rehab timing comes before a stabilized hold loan — without invented DSCR floors or close guarantees.
descriptions./resources/commercial-docs/: What a commercial loan file actually requires: rent roll, T-12, leases, and entity documents, and why each one drives the underwriting on income property.
descriptions./resources/construction-budget/: How to build a construction budget that underwrites: hard costs vs soft costs, the draw schedule, and why ground-up projects need a real contingency line.
descriptions./resources/debt-vs-jv/: Keep all the profit with debt, or share the economics with a partner who funds the deal. When each one wins, the real trade-offs, and how the shared-economics structure fits.
descriptions./resources/dscr-explained/: What debt-service coverage ratio is, how it is calculated from a rental's income and expenses, why lenders use it, and what different ratios actually mean.
descriptions./resources/fix-and-flip-vs-purchase-reha: How to tell whether a value-add deal is a fix-and-flip sale path or a purchase-and-rehab capital plan — exit, scope, draws, and contribution without 100% or 70% ARV marketing claims.
descriptions./resources/: Plain-English guides to ARV, DSCR, rehab draws, path choice, bridge-to-DSCR, and preparing a deal file. Built for real-estate investors, not lenders.
descriptions./resources/preparing-a-deal-submission/: Exactly what to gather for a fast first read on a real-estate deal: the basis, the budget, ARV support, the exit, and proof of funds, and how each is used.
descriptions./resources/proof-of-funds/: What proof of funds means in investment real estate, what sellers and title actually look for, and how to prepare without oversharing.
descriptions./resources/rehab-draws/: How the rehab draw process works: why renovation funds release against completed work, how inspections verify progress, and how to keep draws moving on schedule.
descriptions./resources/understanding-arv/: What after-repair value means for investment purchases and rehabs — comps, condition, and how cost-to-ARV affects private-lender leverage discussions.
descriptions./resources/which-financing-path/: A practical framework for choosing among fix-and-flip, purchase-and-rehab, bridge, DSCR rental, 2–4 unit, and ground-up paths — without invented rate sheets.
descriptions./resources/why-deals-delay/: The real causes of closing delays: incomplete files, unsupported ARV, title problems, and valuation surprises, plus how to prevent each before it costs you time.
descriptions./services/: RECR services for real-estate investors — capital path review, program matching, file preparation guidance, and partner coordination.
descriptions./south-florida-real-estate-investor-fina: Financing guidance for Fort Lauderdale and South Florida real estate investors across fix-and-flip, DSCR rental, bridge, construction, 2–4 unit and purchase-rehab transactions.
descriptions./submit-a-deal/: Submit a real-estate investment opportunity for preliminary capital-path review with RECR.
descriptions./team/: The people behind Real Estate Capital Resources — capital path guidance for investors in Cleveland and South Florida.
descriptions./terms/: Terms of use for the Real Estate Capital Resources website.
descriptions./tools/cap-rate/: Free cap rate calculator for commercial and multifamily property. Enter annual rent, operating expenses, and price to get NOI and capitalization rate instantly.
descriptions./tools/cash-flow/: Estimate monthly and annual rental cash flow and cash-on-cash return. Enter rent, P&I, taxes, insurance, HOA, plus vacancy, maintenance, and management.
descriptions./tools/checklist/: Documents and details to prepare before a real-estate capital review — preliminary vs full underwriting checklist for investors.
descriptions./tools/deal-analyzer/: Estimate net profit, profit margin, and ROI on a fix-and-flip. Enter purchase, rehab, ARV, holding, and selling costs to see if the spread supports the deal.
descriptions./tools/deal-path/: Guided deal readiness for investment-property financing conversations — which RECR path to discuss and what to have ready. Not a loan approval or quote.
descriptions./tools/dscr/: Free DSCR calculator for rental property. Enter rent and PITIA to get your debt service coverage ratio to two decimals, plus a plain-English verdict.
descriptions./tools/: Free real-estate investor calculators — deal path guidance, DSCR, MAO, cap rate, cash flow, and rehab budgeting — to build the numbers a deal review needs.
descriptions./tools/mao/: Free maximum allowable offer calculator. Enter ARV, rehab, and your percentage to see the highest price a flip can support — and how it maps to the 70% gate.
descriptions./tools/proof-of-funds/: What proof of funds is, when real estate investors need it, what a compliant POF letter contains, and how RECR handles it on a reviewed and funded deal.
descriptions./tools/rehab-budget/: Build a line-item renovation budget by trade — demo, roof, kitchen, bath, mechanical, flooring, exterior — plus a contingency that sums to a defensible total.
